title: Schema: bodyMarkus, bodyIr, aliases, metadata on Item and PublishedItem
description:
## Goal
Add the four content fields from docs/standard-site.md section 1.8 to the `Item` and `PublishedItem` models and thread them through the Python authoring client and the TypeScript GraphQL types. Additive only: no behavior changes, nothing reads them yet.

| Field | AppSync type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bodyMarkus` | `String` | Article body in Anthus Markus source (body only: the text after the front matter; includes `::image{}`, `[@key]`, `::citations{}` and Markus directives). Source of truth. |
| `bodyIr` | `AWSJSON` | Derived envelope (see `PPY-e169c5`), written only by the save/validate step, never by hand. |
| `aliases` | `[String]` | Legacy URL paths that must 301 to this item (e.g. `/blog/old-slug`). |
| `metadata` | `AWSJSON` | `{ "frontMatterYaml": "<raw YAML string>", "source": { "path": "articles/foo.md" }, ... }`; shapes owned by `PPY-22a3b4` / `PPY-b3a10e`. |

The legacy `body: [String]` stays in the schema until the production data is converted (`PPY-cddfb8`, then a later removal ticket in Phase 4; changing it now would break live p.apyr.us).

## Context (verified)
- The deployed schema is `amplify/data/schema.ts` (`export const schema = a.schema({...})`, used by `defineData` in `amplify/data/resource.ts` L2127-2140). `amplify/data/resource.ts` ALSO holds a full duplicate `a.schema` (L28-2112) whose `Schema` type (L2122, `ClientSchema<typeof schema>`) is what `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` L2 and most handlers import. Both define `Item` and `PublishedItem` with identical fields: `schema.ts` L1581-1620 (Item), L1750-1790 (PublishedItem); `resource.ts` L1717-1760 (Item), L1922-1960 (PublishedItem). They must be edited together or typed clients and the deployed API drift.
- Python field lists: `src/papyrus_content/graphql_authoring.py` L121-128: `ITEM_FIELDS` and `PUBLISHED_ITEM_FIELDS` (GraphQL selection strings used by `list_records`, `get_record`, mutations via `LIST_DEFINITIONS`/`MUTATIONS`).
- TS read types: `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` L64-83 `GraphQLItem`. Other writers of `Item`/`PublishedItem`: `amplify/seed/seed.ts` (upserts at L558, L635), `src/papyrus_content/seed_edition.py` (`seed_article_records`, L223-300), `scripts/content-cli.cjs` (legacy JS CLI; L11598, L12641), `src/papyrus_content/rehydration_commands.py` L50-154 (lists `("PublishedItem", "body")` for rehydration), `src/papyrus_content/model_attachments.py` L190-330 (body -> attachment expansion for `Item`/`PublishedItem`).
- AGENTS.md "Schema and API alignment": do not add runtime shims for schema drift; deploy the schema to the sandbox.

## Exact changes
1. `amplify/data/schema.ts` and `amplify/data/resource.ts`: in `Item` (after `body: a.string().array(),`) and in `PublishedItem` (same position) add
   ```ts
   bodyMarkus: a.string(),
   bodyIr: a.json(),
   aliases: a.string().array(),
   metadata: a.json(),
   ```
2. `src/papyrus_content/graphql_authoring.py`: append ` bodyMarkus bodyIr aliases metadata` to `ITEM_FIELDS` and `PUBLISHED_ITEM_FIELDS`. Do not touch `strip_unsupported_payload_fields`.
3. `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` `GraphQLItem`: add `bodyMarkus?: string | null; bodyIr?: unknown; aliases?: Array<string | null> | null; metadata?: unknown;` (typing only; `PPY-cddfb8` consumes them).
4. `src/papyrus_content/model_attachments.py` and `rehydration_commands.py`: read the body-attachment expansion; confirm it only touches `body` and that records carrying `bodyMarkus`/`bodyIr` pass through `expand_private_payload_records` (L295) unchanged. Add a unit test for that (below). If it would move `bodyMarkus` into an attachment, change it to leave the new fields inline (inline storage is the decision; DynamoDB limit is 400 KB per item, see `PPY-e169c5` size guard).
5. `scripts/test-schema-parity.ts` (new, run with `npx tsx`; add npm script `test:schema-parity`): imports `schema` from `amplify/data/schema.ts` and the duplicate from `amplify/data/resource.ts` is not exported, so parse both files' `Item`/`PublishedItem` blocks textually (regex between `Item:`/`PublishedItem:` and the next `.secondaryIndexes`) and assert the sets of field names are equal across the two files and include the four new fields. Fails when someone edits one file only.

## Data shapes
GraphQL after deploy: `type Item { ... body: [String] bodyMarkus: String bodyIr: AWSJSON aliases: [String] metadata: AWSJSON ... }` and the same on `PublishedItem`; matching `CreateItemInput`/`UpdateItemInput`/`ModelItemFilterInput`. Python writes JSON fields as strings via `seed_edition.to_aws_json(value)` (`json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"))`).

## Tests
- `npx tsx scripts/test-schema-parity.ts` (new) and `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_content_item_fields.py` (new, unittest): (a) `ITEM_FIELDS`/`PUBLISHED_ITEM_FIELDS` contain the four names; (b) `expand_private_payload_records([{"modelName":"Item","expected":{...,"bodyMarkus":"x","bodyIr":"{}"}}])` returns the record with both fields intact.
- Sandbox check (needs AWS; follow `AGENTS.local.md`): `npx ampx sandbox` then `poetry run papyrus content schema-check --type Item --fields bodyMarkus,bodyIr,aliases,metadata` and the same for `PublishedItem` print `schema-check\tok\ttrue`.
- No Gherkin (data plumbing).

## Acceptance checks
- `npx tsx scripts/test-schema-parity.ts` exits 0; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_content_item_fields -v` passes.
- Sandbox: the two `schema-check` commands exit 0.

## Dependencies
None. Runs in parallel with `PPY-e169c5` (pure Python). Blocks `PPY-b3a10e`, `PPY-cddfb8`, `PPY-22a3b4`, `PPY-1d0f3d`, `PPY-3e5235` (they write/read the fields on a deployed API). Same-file conflicts: `amplify/data/schema.ts` and `resource.ts` are also edited by `PPY-3e5235` (new GraphQL operations) — land SCH first, LMB rebases.

## Risks
- Deploying to production changes the live p.apyr.us/Pilobol AppSync schema (additive, safe) but must go through the normal `main` pipeline; agents never deploy production. Items without the fields are fine (all four nullable).
- The duplicate schema in `resource.ts` is a maintenance trap; the parity test is the guard. Do not refactor it away in this ticket.

## Needs Ryan
Only the eventual promotion `develop -> main` of the batch of Phase 2 backend changes (his decision, not part of this ticket).

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-44a0f9-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
